question: What content-policy category boundaries and default consequences should ClawHub adopt for spam, crypto/blockchain/finance/trade, malicious scan outcomes, and positive trust signals?
rationale: This is a registry trust and enforcement boundary, and current code/docs provide adjacent scanner behavior but not the final policy choices or public/private split.

options.title: Accept As Policy Work
options.body: Publish a category-to-consequence matrix plus allowed/not-allowed/edge-case examples, while keeping scanner thresholds and reviewer-only tactics in specs or internal runbooks.

options.title: Split Crypto/Trust Sub-RFCs
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but move crypto/payment exceptions and positive trust signals into narrower RFCs before publishing final public policy.

options.title: Defer Public Matrix
options.body: Leave current broad acceptable-use and scanner guidance in place and keep category consequences as case-by-case maintainer judgment for now.

recommendation.title: Accept As Policy Work
recommendation.body: Publish a category-to-consequence matrix plus allowed/not-allowed/edge-case examples, while keeping scanner thresholds and reviewer-only tactics in specs or internal runbooks.
